text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers:
- The United States on Thursday announced it favoured the admission of only three ex-communist states to NATO in the first round of its extension, thus excluding Slovenia and Romania.

- 22 pupils and four teachers of an elementary school in Ljubljana were injured on Thursday, when their bus with 48 children on board crashed into a house. Two pupils and the driver were seriously injured in the accident.

- Slovenian Defence Minister Tit Turnsek said that a U.S. decision to exclude Slovenia from the first round of NATO expansion would not necessarily win backing from European states that have said they back Slovenian entry.
- The Slovenian government said on Thursday it had prepared legislation on foreign exchange transactions aimed at bringing the country's laws into line with EU regulations.
- A second group of Slovenian soldiers returned from an artillery exercise in Hungary, Slovenia's first army exercise abroad.

- Slovenia has the support of at least nine alliance member states for its candidature for NATO membership and this support is getting stronger. Other NATO members are not opposed to Slovenia joining, said Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler. He underlined that Slovenia would continue in its bid for NATO membership.
- Central bank governors of Slovenia, Croatia and Macedonia said that they will propose a meeting with the governor of Yugoslavia's central bank to discuss the new status of central banks.
- A Slovenian army commission, investigating an accident in April that left one soldier dead and two seriously injured, said the reason for the accident was human error.
- Slovenia signed a 400 million mark seven-year Eurobond issue deal. Joint lead managers for the transaction were CSFB and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, the finance ministry said on Thursday.
